Lately, I’ve just been… all over the place. For about a month last year, I was running on three hours of sleep and didn’t even notice—I was coding through the night, jumping between cloud infrastructures like I was chasing something. I wasn’t tired, just wired. I remember talking nonstop in meetings, cutting people off, getting annoyed if someone didn’t get my ideas right away. I even hooked up with someone from work, which wasn’t like me—normally I’m more careful. But honestly, it didn’t feel out of control at the time. I was just *doing*.

But that passed. For most of the past year, it’s been the opposite. I’ll sit at my desk and just… freeze. Can’t focus on a single architecture diagram without feeling completely drained. Some days I cry out of nowhere—on the train, in the bathroom at work. I’ve stopped replying to friends’ texts. I just don’t have the energy. I’ll think, “What’s the point of any of this?” Not that I’d ever do anything, but… I wouldn’t mind if I didn’t wake up.

I don’t know if this is ADHD, or mood swings, or just burnout. I’ve always had bursts of energy, but not like this. And the low periods—those aren’t new, either. I can’t say anything started exactly in childhood. It’s all just… blurry.

D009-D001_h014.question_both:
I’ve been feeling... off… for quite some time—almost a year now. Most days, I’m just wiped out. My body feels like it’s made of concrete, even if I’ve done nothing. I wake up after nightmares, cold and shaky, and sometimes I just end up crying in the dark. It’s been worse lately, though it’s not like there’s anything specific to cry about—just this heaviness.

But then last month, for about three weeks, it was like someone flipped a switch. I wasn’t tired at all. I started calling old coworkers, even people I haven’t spoken to in years, just to talk, to plan things—we should start that band, why not launch a security training course? I felt sharp, unstoppable. I walked miles without noticing, cleaned out storage rooms at work, rearranged my apartment at 2 a.m. Just couldn't sit still.

Thing is, I don’t know if this is all connected. The energy surge didn’t ruin anything—at work I didn’t mess up—but now I’m back to dragging through shifts, barely holding on. I’ve always been restless, I guess, but I can’t say if that started as a kid or just… showed up later. And the quiet years in between? They blur together.
D009-D001_h014.question_a:
I’ve been a night watchman for over twenty years, ever since my wife passed. Lately, things have been… all over the place. For about three weeks this spring, I suddenly felt like I’d been plugged into a live wire. I wasn’t tired at all—slept maybe four hours and still felt great. My mind would race with ideas, like I could solve any problem, fix anything. I started calling up old friends out of the blue, even went to a bar one night and was talking to strangers—completely unlike me. I took on extra shifts, cleaned the entire house on my days off, just couldn’t sit still. But oddly, I didn’t screw anything up, didn’t get in trouble—just felt powerful, unstoppable.

Then that passed, and for the next nine months, it was like the opposite. I’d wake up already exhausted, body so heavy I could barely stand. Cried a lot—didn’t know why, just a deep sadness. I kept having the same nightmare—my wife, falling away into darkness. I called in sick a few times, couldn’t face anyone.

The key is, those restless, sped-up thoughts—the not needing sleep, the talking fast, the can’t-stop moving—only happened during that brief high spell. Never before, not since. Definitely not since I was a kid.
D009-D001_h014.question_b:
I’ve been working nights for over 30 years now—quiet shifts give me time to think, or at least they used to. Truth is, I’ve never really sat still my whole life. Even as a kid, my teachers said I couldn’t focus, always fidgeting, blurting out answers. I thought it was just how I was wired. But lately… it’s like those old restlessness and racing thoughts have gotten louder. For about three weeks, I felt *unstoppable*—not sleeping more than three hours a night, talking so fast my dispatcher complained she couldn’t get a word in, jumping from one task to another, even calling up old friends out of the blue. I felt like I could run the whole security company single-handed.  

But that passed. Since my wife passed two years ago, things got darker. For most of the last nine months, I’ve been drained—my legs feel like concrete, I cry over small things, and I dread sleep because the nightmares come: falling, losing people. I can’t concentrate on my rounds. The thing is, the fidgeting, the distractibility, the not sleeping… that’s been with me since *before* I was twelve, long before any of these mood swings. It’s always been me.
